name: Verapamil
summary: A non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker with strong cardiac (AV nodal) effects; first-line for terminating paroxysmal SVT and used for rate control, angina, and hypertension.
mechanism: Blocks L-type calcium channels in cardiac myocytes and the SA/AV nodes, slowing conduction and automaticity while vasodilating arterioles.

dosing.adult: Hypertension: extended-release 180–240 mg once daily; PSVT: IV 5 mg over 2 min (repeat 5–10 mg if needed)

warnings: Negative inotrope — can precipitate heart failure
Raises digoxin levels (~50–70%) — monitor digoxin concentrations
CYP3A4 inhibition increases levels of simvastatin, cyclosporine, and others
Hypotension and bradycardia, especially with IV use
safety.overdose: Severe bradycardia, AV block, hypotension, asystole; treat with calcium gluconate, atropine, and pacing.

clinicalPearls: Constipation is the classic nuisance side effect, more than with diltiazem.
The digoxin interaction is the one to remember — levels can rise by half, so halve digoxin or monitor levels.
good: SVT termination and hypertension-plus-angina patients with preserved EF.
bad: HFrEF, AV block, or patients on digoxin without level monitoring.
